t: How to Create Your First Thrive Apprentice Course
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to set up Thrive Apprentice for the first time and create your first online course—from initial configuration to publishing your first lesson.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice installed and activated on your WordPress site.
  • The Thrive Product Manager used to install the plugin (available from your Thrive Themes account).

Accessing Thrive Apprentice

  1. Log in to your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Hover over Thrive Dashboard in the left sidebar menu.
  3. Click Thrive Apprentice.

Tip: You can also access Thrive Apprentice by navigating to the Thrive Dashboard page and clicking the Thrive Apprentice card.

Running the Setup Wizard

If this is your first time opening Thrive Apprentice, a setup wizard will appear automatically.

  1. Click Get Started on the welcome lightbox.
  2. On the next screen, choose where your courses will be displayed: - Select an existing page from the dropdown, or - Click Add New Page to create a dedicated courses page.
  3. Click Save and Continue to confirm your selection.

Note: The page you select (or create) becomes your main Courses page—the public-facing page where visitors can browse all available courses.

Creating Your First Course

Once the setup wizard is complete, you'll land on the Thrive Apprentice dashboard.

  1. Click the Courses tab in the left sidebar.
  2. Click the Add Course button at the top of the page.
  3. Enter a Course Title (e.g., "Introduction to Email Marketing").
  4. Optionally, add a Course Description to explain what students will learn.
  5. Click Save to create the course.

Your new course is now visible in the course list.

Adding Modules and Chapters

Modules and chapters help you organize your course content into logical sections.

  1. Open your course by clicking on it in the Courses list.
  2. Click Add Module to create a top-level section (e.g., "Module 1: The Basics").
  3. Enter a Module Title and click Save.
  4. To add chapters within a module, click Add Chapter underneath the module.

Tip: Modules are optional—you can add lessons directly to a course without modules if your content doesn't need that level of organization.

Adding Your First Lesson

  1. Inside your course (or within a module), click Add Lesson.
  2. Enter a Lesson Title.
  3. Click Save to create the lesson.
  4. To add content to the lesson, click Edit Content—this opens the lesson in Thrive Architect, where you can add text, images, videos, and other elements.
  5. When you're done editing, click Save Work in Thrive Architect, then click Done to return to Thrive Apprentice.

Publishing Your Course

By default, new courses are set to Draft status. To make your course available to students:

  1. Go back to the Courses tab.
  2. Hover over your course and click Edit.
  3. Change the Course Status to Published.
  4. Click Save.

Important: Publishing a course makes it visible on your courses page. If you want to restrict access (e.g., paid courses), set up a Product with access rules before publishing. See the Access Restrictions and Rules guide for details.

That's it! You've successfully created your first Thrive Apprentice course, added modules and lessons, and published it for your students.

t: How to Use Course Content Types, Navigation, and Progress Tracking in Thrive Apprentice
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to organize your Thrive Apprentice courses using the four content types, understand how navigation works for your students, and see how the progress section tracks their advancement through your course material.

Understanding the Four Content Types

Thrive Apprentice uses a hierarchical structure with four content types that let you organize your course material from broad to specific:

  • Course — The top-level container that holds all of your content. Every piece of material lives inside a course.
  • Module — An optional organizational layer that groups related chapters or lessons together (e.g., "Module 1: The Basics").
  • Chapter — A sub-section within a module (or directly within a course) that groups related lessons together.
  • Lesson — The individual content unit where students consume your material—text, video, quizzes, and more.

Tip: You don't have to use every level. A simple course can contain just lessons, while a comprehensive certification program might use all four levels. Choose the structure that best fits your content.

Structuring Your Course Hierarchy

When building a course, think of the hierarchy as a nesting system. Here's how the levels relate to each other:

  1. Create a Course as the outermost container.
  2. Add Modules inside the course to divide it into major topics or units.
  3. Add Chapters inside modules to break topics into smaller groups.
  4. Add Lessons inside chapters (or directly inside modules or the course itself) for the actual learning content.

For example, a photography course might look like this:

  • Course: Mastering Digital Photography - Module 1: Camera Fundamentals - Chapter 1: Understanding Your Equipment - Lesson 1: Camera Body and Lens Basics - Lesson 2: Aperture, Shutter Speed, and ISO - Chapter 2: Shooting Modes - Lesson 3: Manual vs. Auto Mode - Module 2: Composition Techniques - Lesson 4: The Rule of Thirds - Lesson 5: Leading Lines and Framing

How Course Navigation Works for Students

Thrive Apprentice automatically generates a navigation sidebar for your students. This sidebar displays the full course structure—modules, chapters, and lessons—so students always know where they are and what comes next.

Key navigation features include:

  • Expandable sections — Students can expand or collapse modules and chapters to focus on the content they need.
  • Next/Previous buttons — Lessons include navigation buttons that move students sequentially through the course.
  • Clickable structure — Students can jump to any unlocked lesson directly from the sidebar.
  • Breadcrumb-style orientation — The current lesson is highlighted in the sidebar so students can see exactly where they are in the overall structure.

How the Progress Section Tracks Student Advancement

The progress section gives students a clear visual indicator of how far they've come and how much remains. Thrive Apprentice tracks progress automatically as students complete lessons.

  • Progress bar — A visual bar shows the percentage of the course the student has completed.
  • Completion checkmarks — Individual lessons display a checkmark once the student has finished them.
  • Module and chapter progress — Higher-level containers show aggregated progress based on the lessons completed within them.
  • Course-level overview — On the course overview page, students can see their total progress at a glance.

Note: Progress is tracked per student, so each logged-in user sees their own completion status. Students must be logged in for progress tracking to work.

Dynamic Labels That Adapt Based on Visitor Access

Thrive Apprentice uses dynamic labels that automatically change based on each visitor's access level. These labels appear alongside courses and lessons to communicate access status without any manual configuration on your part.

Depending on the visitor's permissions, they may see labels such as:

  • Free — The content is available to anyone without restrictions.
  • Login Required — The visitor needs to log in to access the course.
  • Purchase Required — The visitor must buy a product to unlock the content.
  • Restricted — The content is not available based on the current access rules.

These labels update dynamically—if a visitor logs in or purchases a product, the labels change to reflect their new access level. This keeps your course pages accurate and personalized without extra work.

That's it! You've successfully learned how to use the four content types to structure your courses, how navigation keeps students oriented, how progress tracking shows their advancement, and how dynamic labels adapt to each visitor's access level.

t: How to Create Course Bundles in Thrive Apprentice
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to create course bundles in Thrive Apprentice—allowing you to package multiple courses together and sell them at a single price point using the Products framework.

What Are Course Bundles?

A course bundle is a collection of two or more courses grouped together and sold as a single product. Bundles let you offer more value to your students at a discounted rate while increasing your revenue per transaction.

For example, if you sell three individual courses at $25 each, you could bundle all three together and offer the package for $60—giving students a $15 discount while earning more per sale than a single course purchase.

Understanding the Products Framework

In Thrive Apprentice, bundles are created through the Products section. A product is the mechanism that protects and sells your content. Products extend beyond just courses—you can use them to bundle courses with pages, posts, and custom content, making it possible to build entire membership websites.

Note: Every piece of content you want to restrict or sell needs to be associated with a product. Think of products as the "access keys" your students purchase to unlock content.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice installed and activated on your WordPress site.
  • At least two published courses ready to bundle together.
  • A payment integration configured if you plan to sell the bundle (e.g., SendOwl, WooCommerce, or ThriveCart).

Creating a Course Bundle Step by Step

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice in your WordPress admin.
  2. Click the Products tab in the left sidebar.
  3. Click the Add New Product button.
  4. Enter a Product Name for your bundle (e.g., "Complete Marketing Mastery Bundle").
  5. Optionally, add a Product Description to explain what's included.
  6. Click Save to create the product.

Adding Courses to the Bundle

Once your product is created, you need to associate your courses with it:

  1. Open the product you just created by clicking on it in the Products list.
  2. Look for the Course Access or Content section within the product settings.
  3. Click Add Course and select the first course you want to include.
  4. Repeat for each additional course you want in the bundle.
  5. Click Save to confirm your selections.

Tip: You can also add pages, posts, and other custom content to the same product—not just courses. This is useful for including bonus materials, resource libraries, or exclusive blog content alongside your courses.

Configuring Access Rules

After adding courses to your bundle, you need to set up access rules so that only students who purchase the product can access the bundled content:

  1. Within the product settings, navigate to the Access Requirements section.
  2. Configure how students gain access—through a direct purchase, a membership, or a manual grant.
  3. Connect your product to a payment gateway if you are selling the bundle (e.g., link to a ThriveCart checkout or a WooCommerce product).
  4. Set any additional restrictions, such as time-limited access or drip-released content.
  5. Click Save to apply the access rules.

Important: When multiple access rules apply to the same piece of content, Thrive Apprentice uses a content protection priority system. The most restrictive rule takes precedence, so review your rules carefully to ensure students get the access they expect.

That's it! You've successfully created a course bundle in Thrive Apprentice, added courses to it, and configured the access rules that control who can unlock the bundled content.

t: How to Create a Free Course Funnel in Thrive Apprentice
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to create a free online course funnel using Thrive Apprentice and Thrive Architect—a proven strategy for building your email list by offering a free course as a lead generation tool.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k4834OYrrNk

What Is a Free Course Funnel?

A free course funnel is a marketing strategy where you offer a free online course in exchange for a visitor's email address. Instead of selling the course directly, you use it as a lead magnet—attracting potential customers, growing your email list, and nurturing them toward purchasing your paid products or services.

Why Use a Free Course Funnel?

Free course funnels are one of the most effective ways to grow your audience because:

  • High perceived value — A free course feels more valuable than a simple PDF download, which increases opt-in rates.
  • Email list building — You collect email addresses from every student who enrolls, giving you a direct line of communication.
  • Trust building — Delivering quality content for free demonstrates your expertise and builds trust with your audience.
  • Upsell opportunities — Once students complete the free course, you can promote your paid courses, memberships, or services.

Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice installed and activated on your WordPress site.
  • Thrive Architect installed for building your landing page.
  • An email marketing service connected to your site (e.g., Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, ConvertKit).

Step 1: Create Your Free Course in Thrive Apprentice

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click the Courses tab in the left sidebar.
  3. Click Add Course and enter a compelling course title.
  4. Add a course description that highlights what students will learn.
  5. Add your lessons with the free content you want to deliver.
  6. Set the Course Status to Published.

Tip: Keep your free course focused and concise—three to five lessons work well. You want to deliver enough value to impress your audience without giving away everything you have to offer.

Step 2: Build a Landing Page with Thrive Architect

  1. Create a new page in WordPress (e.g., "Free Course: [Your Topic]").
  2. Click Launch Thrive Architect to open the visual editor.
  3. Choose a landing page template or start from scratch.
  4. Add a headline that clearly states the benefit of the free course.
  5. Include bullet points listing what students will learn.
  6. Add social proof elements if available (testimonials, student count, etc.).

Step 3: Configure Access—No Product or Payment Needed

Since this is a free course, you don't need to create a product or connect a payment gateway. You simply need to ensure students can access the course after providing their email:

  1. In Thrive Apprentice, make sure the course is not linked to any paid product.
  2. Set the course access to allow any logged-in user to view the content.
  3. New students will be created as WordPress users when they opt in through your form.

Step 4: Set Up the Opt-In Form

  1. In Thrive Architect, add a Lead Generation element to your landing page.
  2. Connect the form to your email marketing service using the API Connection settings.
  3. Configure the form fields—at minimum, collect the student's Name and Email Address.
  4. Set the After Submission action to redirect students to the course page or a thank-you page with a link to the course.

Note: Make sure the opt-in form creates a WordPress user account so the student can log in and access the course content in Thrive Apprentice.

Step 5: Connect Your Email Service

  1. Go to Thrive Dashboard > API Connections.
  2. Click Add New Connection and select your email service provider.
  3. Enter your API key or credentials and click Connect.
  4. Return to your landing page and link the opt-in form to the appropriate email list or tag.

Step 6: Test the Funnel

Before promoting your funnel, test every step of the process:

  1. Visit your landing page as a logged-out user.
  2. Submit the opt-in form with a test email address.
  3. Confirm you receive the email in your email marketing service.
  4. Verify the redirect takes you to the course or thank-you page.
  5. Log in as the test user and confirm you can access all course lessons.

Important: Test from an incognito or private browser window to simulate a first-time visitor's experience accurately.

That's it! You've successfully created a free course funnel that captures leads, grows your email list, and delivers valuable content to your new subscribers automatically.
